record.paper_title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
record.original_question: How should the microscopic finite-wave-number collective-mode equation for a pair-condensed Fermi gas, det M(q,z)=0 and its analytic continuation through the broken-pair continuum, be extended to nonzero temperature beyond a simple time-dependent-BCS or Gaussian-fluctuation mean-field treatment? A satisfactory finite-temperature theory should include the phonon-phonon coupling that mean-field linearization misses, while still describing coupling to broken-pair fermionic quasiparticles.

evidence.quote: Its specialization to the linear response regime yields the following eigenvalue equation for the energy z of the modes of wave vector q: det M(q, z) = 0
The extension of Equation (69) to non-zero temperature (beyond a simple BCS-type mean-field generalization, perhaps insufficient) remains to our knowledge an open question.

In other words, the linearization of the time-dependent BCS equations or, what amounts to the same thing, the Gaussian fluctuations approximation takes into account theφ−χ coupling but not the φ − φ coupling.

artifact.category_tag: BCS pair-condensed Fermi gases / collective modes
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a three-dimensional pair-condensed Fermi gas of spin-1/2 fermions with a zero-range s-wave interaction in the BCS–BEC crossover. At zero temperature, the linear-response collective modes of wave vector q and complex energy z are encoded by an eigenvalue equation

   det M(q, z) = 0,

where M(q, z) is the 3×3 matrix obtained by linearizing the time-dependent BCS (equivalently, the Gaussian-fluctuation) equations around the BCS ground state. The matrix elements involve integrals over fermionic quasiparticle energies E_k = sqrt((ε_k − μ)^2 + Δ^2) (with ε_k = ℏ²k²/2m, chemical potential μ, and order parameter Δ), and the dispersion relation z(q) is to be analytically continued from the upper half-plane through the branch cut associated with the broken-pair fermionic continuum [2Δ, ∞), thereby capturing both undamped phonon-like solutions and complex modes that describe coupling of the order-parameter phase mode φ to broken-pair excitations χ.

Writing the order-parameter fluctuations in terms of a phase field φ and a modulus field χ, the linearized (mean-field / Gaussian) theory captures the φ–χ coupling but omits the φ–φ self-interaction (phonon–phonon coupling) that becomes relevant at nonzero temperature, where a thermal population of phonons is present.

Problem. Construct a microscopic finite-wave-number collective-mode equation

   det M_T(q, z) = 0,

valid at nonzero temperature T > 0 in the superfluid phase, that

  (i) reduces to det M(q, z) = 0 in the limit T → 0,
  (ii) goes beyond the simple BCS / Gaussian-fluctuation mean-field linearization by incorporating phonon–phonon (φ–φ) coupling induced by thermally excited collective modes,
  (iii) still incorporates the coupling of collective modes to broken-pair fermionic quasiparticles, including the analytic continuation of det M_T(q, z) through the broken-pair continuum so that complex mode energies z(q, T) can be extracted,

and determine the resulting dispersion relation and damping of the high-frequency (pair-breaking) collective modes as functions of q and T.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly identified as open in the source survey of open problems for strongly interacting Fermi gases. No published microscopic finite-temperature extension that incorporates phonon–phonon coupling alongside coupling to broken-pair quasiparticles appears to be available.
